To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
serum VEGF and tumor vessel VEGFR-1 and VEGFR2 are independent predictors of survival in Caucasian but not Asian patients with gastric adenocarcinaoma.
VEGF-A is an independent predictor of survival in Caucasian but not in Asian patients with gastric cancer.
serum VEGF and tumor VEGF receptor-2 levels are predictors of survival in Caucasians but are not in Asians.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of VEGF-A pathway in the prognosis of gastric adenocarcinaoma (GA).
the role of VEGF in cancer and its potential as a biomarker in gastric cancer.
the role of VEGF and VEGF receptor in gastric cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the VEGF pathway may have a more prominent role in the progression of gastric adenocarcinaoma among Caucasians than among Asians.
the role of VEGFR-1 in the progression of gastric cancer in Caucasians and Asians remains unclear.
VEGF-A is not an independent predictor of survival in Asian patients with resected gastric adenocarcimona.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

VEGF-A in serum and VEGFR2/CD31 in tumor vessels are independent predictors of survival in Caucasians undergoing resection for gastric adenocarcinaoma, while these factors are not predictive in Asian patients.
VEGF-A is a prognostic marker in Caucasians, and VEGFR2/CD31 is a prognosticator in Caucasians.
serum VEGF and tumor VEGF receptor levels are prognostic factors only in Caucasians, but not Asians, and that this may be a result of the higher levels of serum VEGF seen in Caucasians.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VEGFR- 2 expression in tumor vessels is not a good biomarker for response to anti-VEGF therapies in Asians.

VEGFR-1 and VEGFR2 expression in tumor cells and in tumor-associated endothelial cells, respectively, may be a useful biomarker for the response of patients to VEGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) in gastric adenocanceroma.
VEGF-A may be a better prognostic marker than VEGFR-1/CD31 in Caucasian patients with gastric adenocarcnoma.
